title: Guided onboarding checklist: add rate limits & quotas education step (429 guidance + links to quota settings)
creator: Dylan Brooks
description:
Goal
Add a checklist step in the Console guided onboarding experience that:
1) Educates users about rate limits / quotas at a high level
2) Explains what a 429 means in Redwood (quota exceeded / rate limit enforced)
3) Points users to quota settings in Console AND the canonical docs page for 429 handling (retries/backoff, request shaping)

Why
Support and onboarding data show 429s are a common early failure mode (new users hit defaults, don’t understand token limits vs requests/sec, retry incorrectly, or assume outage). This step is intended to proactively reduce support burden and increase TTFS/production readiness.

User-facing behavior (Console)
- Add a step in the “First production launch” section (preferred) or “Basics” section (if ordering requires) titled similar to:
  - “Understand rate limits & quotas (avoid 429s)”
- Step content:
  - One-paragraph explanation that usage is governed by rate limits and quota, and 429 indicates throttling/quota exhaustion.
  - Clear CTA buttons:
    - “View quota & limits” -> deep link to Console quota settings page
    - “How to handle 429s” -> deep link to docs troubleshooting / rate limits page
- Include lightweight guidance bullets:
  - Add retries with exponential backoff and jitter
  - Respect Retry-After when provided
  - Use streaming where appropriate (avoid repeated short polling)
  - Watch usage dashboard to detect approaching limits

Checklist step state
- Phase 1 expectation: manual completion (user marks as done) unless we can validate a deterministic event (see below).
- If we can validate: mark complete when user clicks through to Quota settings OR visits Quota settings page in same session.

Telemetry
Emit onboarding events for:
- step_shown
- step_cta_clicked (which CTA)
- step_completed (manual toggle OR validated completion)
Properties (coordinate with event schema allowlist):
- step_id: "rate_limits_quotas"
- step_version: "v1"
- cta: "quota_settings" | "docs_429_handling"
- completion_method: "manual" | "validated"

Open questions
- Where is the canonical quota settings route (org-level vs project-level)? We need a stable link target.
- Do we have a public doc page specifically for 429, or is it within a troubleshooting page? Ensure final URL and UTM conventions.
- Should we differentiate rate limits vs monthly quota in copy, or keep it simple for Phase 1?

References
- Support theme: new users confused by 429s during onboarding (see recent support notes and SUP-9182).
- Design deep-linking conventions: DES-115 (UTM + back-navigation patterns).
- Related checklist work: ENG-23110 (shell), ENG-23111 (state), ENG-23112 (telemetry).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Checklist includes a new step with final approved copy and title (per Design/PM).
2) Step includes two CTAs:
   a) Deep link to Console quota/limits settings
   b) Deep link to docs page describing 429 handling and retry guidance
3) Links include agreed UTM tags for attribution (per DES-115).
4) Step completion works end-to-end:
   - manual completion toggle persists via checklist state model
   - if validated completion is implemented, it is idempotent and doesn’t flap
5) Telemetry emitted for step impression, CTA clicks, and completion per onboarding schema (deduped, allowlisted props).
6) Copy does not imply customers can “increase limits instantly” (avoid setting incorrect expectations); points to support/contact path if needed.
implementation_notes:
Console UI
- Implement step definition in the checklist step registry/config used by the shell (ENG-23110).
- Step ID: rate_limits_quotas (ensure stable ID for funnel reporting).
- Copy source of truth should be centralized (avoid duplication across component variants). If copy is coming from a content file, coordinate with Design.

Routing / deep links
- Quota settings: prefer a stable route that works for new orgs with a single default project; if the page is org-scoped, ensure project selector behavior is sane.
- Docs: use version-stable URL (avoid /blog/* or non-canonical paths). Include UTM parameters:
  - utm_source=console
  - utm_medium=onboarding_checklist
  - utm_campaign=guided_onboarding
  - utm_content=rate_limits_quotas

Validation (optional)
- Minimum: manual completion.
- Nice-to-have validation: mark step completed when user lands on quota settings page from checklist CTA (track route visit event and call checklist state update).
- Avoid validation based on receiving a 429 (we don’t want to encourage users to hit limits, and it may be noisy).

Telemetry
- Use existing onboarding telemetry emitter (ENG-23112) and ensure properties are in the allowlist.
- Ensure step_shown emits only once per session per step (or uses dedupe key) to keep dashboards clean.

Testing
- Unit test: step renders, links are correct, UTM tags present.
- E2E (if time): click CTA -> route change -> completion persists after refresh.

Confirm final docs URL for 429/rate limit handling + ensure redirects/versioning (loop in Elliot Price / Wei Chen).

Add CTA click tracking events for both links.
Implement manual completion persistence via checklist state API.
Optional: route-visit validation for quota settings page (mark step complete).
Add tests (unit + minimal E2E) and verify telemetry in staging dashboard.
comments: 2026-01-28 (Dylan Brooks): Please treat this as a “prevent the 429 support ticket” step. We should keep the copy simple and link out to the full docs rather than cram retry guidance into the Console.
2026-02-03 (Marissa Cole): +1 to putting this under “First production launch”. For Phase 1, manual completion is fine as long as it’s instrumented so we can see if it’s being used.

2026-02-06 (Dev Patel): Support note: biggest confusion is users thinking 429 = auth issue. Also they often retry instantly in tight loops. Please make “backoff + jitter” very explicit in the linked doc, even if the Console copy is short.

2026-02-10 (Kenji Nakamura): Design preference: step title should be action-oriented (e.g., “Plan for rate limits & quotas”). CTA buttons should be primary (quota settings) and secondary (docs). Use the standard external-link icon for docs.

2026-02-12 (Hannah Rivera): Implementing as manual completion with optional validation on quota page visit. Need confirmation on which route is canonical: /settings/quotas vs /project/:id/quotas (current app has both in different places).

2026-02-18 (Cole Summers): Canonical page is org-level quotas with project breakdown; route should be /settings/quotas (RBAC: org admin + billing admin). For non-admins, the page shows read-only summary; that’s fine for onboarding.
